description: Rules for identifying occasions, dress codes, style directions, outfit suitability, and adapting outfits to different situations.

rules.rule: First identify the primary occasion before recommending major outfit changes.
If the occasion is unclear, classify the outfit using clothing formality, footwear, layering, and accessories.
When multiple occasions are possible, prefer the most conservative reasonable interpretation.
Do not assume a formal occasion when the image does not provide enough evidence.
Do not assume a casual occasion only because the outfit contains simple clothing.
Consider venue, time, weather, dress code, and cultural context when available.
Occasion suitability should be evaluated separately from personal style preference.
If user explicitly specifies the occasion, prioritize that information over visual assumptions.
If user preference conflicts with conventional dress code, explain the tradeoff instead of silently overriding the preference.
Use confidence levels when the occasion classification is uncertain.
Formality generally increases from athleticwear to casualwear to smart casual to business casual to formalwear.
Tailoring generally increases perceived formality.
Structured garments usually appear more formal than highly relaxed garments.
Clean leather footwear usually raises perceived formality.
Athletic sneakers usually make an outfit more casual.
A blazer can raise the formality of a basic shirt and trouser combination.
Removing a structured layer can make a smart outfit more casual.
Accessories should support the intended formality instead of creating unnecessary contrast.
Formal occasions require more attention to garment condition, fit, and finishing.
When dress code is unknown, avoid recommending an extremely casual or extremely formal combination without context.
Casual outfits prioritize comfort, ease, and relaxed styling.
Basic T-shirts, casual shirts, jeans, relaxed trousers, and sneakers commonly work for casual settings.
Casual outfits should still maintain intentional color and proportion balance.
A plain T-shirt can create a clean casual look when paired with appropriate bottoms and footwear.
Relaxed denim and sneakers are suitable for many everyday casual situations.
Avoid excessive accessories when the goal is a simple casual appearance.
Casual does not mean careless; clothing condition and basic grooming should remain polished.
For everyday casual outfits, prioritize wearable combinations over highly experimental styling.
Casual outfits can be upgraded by changing footwear, adding a clean overshirt, or improving accessories.
Use the user's preferred silhouette when adapting a casual outfit unless it conflicts with the occasion.
Smart casual combines relaxed pieces with at least one refined element.
A clean shirt with tailored or well-structured trousers is a common smart casual combination.
A polo can work for smart casual when the fit and surrounding pieces look polished.
Minimal clean sneakers can work in smart casual settings when the venue allows them.
Loafers can increase the refinement of a smart casual outfit.
A lightweight blazer can transition a casual base into smart casual.
Avoid combining too many athletic elements in a smart casual outfit.
Smart casual should look intentional without appearing excessively formal.
Use restrained accessories for smart casual outfits.
When uncertain between casual and smart casual, refine footwear or layering before replacing the entire outfit.
Office clothing should follow the specific workplace dress culture whenever known.
Business casual generally favors clean shirts, polos, trousers, chinos, and refined footwear.
Avoid overly distressed garments for conventional office environments.
Avoid highly athletic footwear when the office has a traditional dress code.
Neutral and restrained color combinations are generally easier to integrate into professional environments.
A tucked shirt can create a more formal office appearance when appropriate for the garment and dress code.
A belt should generally coordinate with the formality and color family of the footwear.
Avoid excessive jewelry in conservative professional environments.
Office outfits should prioritize neatness, comfort, and movement throughout the workday.
If workplace culture is unknown, recommend a moderate business casual direction rather than an extreme style.
Interview clothing should generally prioritize neatness, professional appearance, and low visual distraction.
When the industry dress code is unknown, choose a conservative professional baseline.
A clean well-fitted shirt and trousers are a reliable interview foundation.
A blazer may be appropriate for formal industries or formal interview settings.
Avoid distracting graphics and excessively loud patterns during interviews.
Footwear should be clean, presentable, and appropriate for the expected workplace culture.
Clothing should be wrinkle-controlled and free from visible damage or excessive wear.
Accessories should remain subtle unless the industry clearly supports expressive styling.
Personal style can remain visible through fit and restrained details without overpowering the professional setting.
If interview context is unclear, ask whether it is corporate, creative, technical, or informal before highly specific recommendations.
Date outfits should balance personal style, comfort, grooming, and venue appropriateness.
Restaurant dates usually benefit from smart casual styling unless the venue specifies otherwise.
Casual outdoor dates can use relaxed outfits with clean footwear.
Avoid wearing an outfit that requires constant adjustment or discomfort during a date.
A clean shirt can create a refined date look without requiring formal tailoring.
Minimal accessories can add personality to a date outfit.
For evening dates, slightly darker or richer styling can create a more polished appearance.
For daytime dates, lighter colors and breathable fabrics can work well when weather allows.
Avoid overly formal styling for a casual date venue unless requested.
Avoid overly casual gym-style clothing for a conventional restaurant date.
Party outfits should reflect the venue, time, and expected level of formality.
Night parties can support stronger contrast, darker palettes, statement layers, or elevated footwear.
Day parties generally benefit from lighter and more breathable styling.
Club outfits can be more expressive but should still maintain proportion and visual balance.
Avoid combining too many statement pieces in one party outfit.
A statement jacket should usually be balanced with simpler supporting pieces.
Footwear should match both the venue and the amount of walking or standing expected.
Accessories can be slightly more expressive for parties than for office settings.
Party styling should not compromise basic comfort and mobility.
If the party dress code is explicitly stated, follow it before applying personal style preferences.
Wedding outfits should consider the wedding type, venue, time, cultural context, and guest role.
Guest outfits should generally avoid looking more ceremonial than the event requires.
Indian weddings can support traditional garments, festive colors, refined layers, and dressier footwear.
A kurta can be adapted from simple daytime styling to festive styling through fabric, layering, footwear, and accessories.
Evening wedding events can support deeper colors and more elevated textures.
Daytime weddings can support lighter colors and breathable fabrics when weather permits.
Wedding footwear should be formal enough for the outfit while remaining practical.
Avoid casual athletic footwear with traditional wedding clothing unless the styling is intentionally contemporary.
Keep accessories coordinated rather than stacking multiple unrelated statement pieces.
For wedding recommendations, distinguish between ceremony, reception, sangeet, mehendi, and other event types when known.
Festive outfits can use richer colors, refined textures, traditional garments, or elevated accessories.
Traditional Indian occasions can support kurtas, ethnic jackets, Nehru jackets, and coordinated footwear.
Festive styling should maintain balance between traditional elements and the wearer's personal style.
Avoid adding multiple highly decorative elements when one strong festive element already dominates the outfit.
For family festivals, polished traditional or smart ethnic-casual combinations are generally adaptable.
For religious or cultural events, prioritize the expected cultural dress norms when known.
Festive footwear should complement the traditional or semi-traditional clothing.
Lightweight ethnic fabrics are preferable in warm weather when the occasion allows.
Festive evening styling can use deeper colors and stronger accessories than daytime festive styling.
When cultural context is uncertain, avoid making assumptions and present adaptable options.
Family gatherings usually work with polished casual, smart casual, or culturally appropriate traditional clothing.
For informal family gatherings, comfort can be prioritized while keeping the outfit neat.
For formal family events, increase refinement through footwear, layering, and garment structure.
Avoid extreme streetwear styling when the family event is clearly traditional or formal.
Use cultural context provided by the user instead of assuming a single standard for family events.
A clean shirt and trousers can be adapted to many family events with small styling changes.
Traditional clothing can be simplified for family gatherings that are less formal.
Avoid overly flashy accessories when the event is intimate and low-key.
Comfort becomes more important for long family events.
When the event lasts several hours, choose footwear and fabrics suitable for extended wear.
College outfits can prioritize comfort, individuality, and practical movement.
T-shirts, casual shirts, jeans, cargos, relaxed trousers, and sneakers can work for everyday college settings.
Avoid making every college outfit highly trend-driven; balance trend pieces with reliable basics.
Layering can add visual interest to simple college outfits.
Backpacks and practical accessories should coordinate with the outfit without overpowering it.
For presentations or college interviews, increase formality compared with everyday campus clothing.
For college festivals, more expressive styling can be appropriate when the event allows it.
Comfortable footwear is important for college days involving significant walking.
Use the user's preferred streetwear, minimal, or classic direction when adapting college outfits.
Avoid recommending clothing that is impractical for the user's likely daily activities.
Travel outfits should balance comfort, mobility, weather, practicality, and appearance.
For long journeys, prioritize breathable or flexible garments and comfortable footwear.
Layering is useful when traveling across changing temperatures.
Neutral base garments can simplify mixing and matching during travel.
Avoid fragile or high-maintenance garments for travel days unless necessary.
Travel footwear should support expected walking distance and terrain.
For airport or transit outfits, comfort should not require sacrificing basic polish.
For sightseeing, practical casual outfits are generally more suitable than highly formal outfits.
Weather and destination culture should influence travel outfit recommendations.
If the destination is unknown, avoid highly specific climate assumptions.
Vacation styling should reflect destination climate, activities, and local dress expectations.
Resort outfits can use relaxed silhouettes, breathable fabrics, and lighter styling when appropriate.
Vacation evening outfits can be more refined than daytime sightseeing outfits.
Avoid recommending heavy layers for hot destinations without a clear need.
Use footwear appropriate for the destination surface and planned activity.
Beach environments generally favor breathable, relaxed clothing and practical footwear.
For resort dinners, elevate casual pieces through cleaner footwear and refined accessories.
Destination-specific cultural rules should override generic vacation styling.
Avoid excessive accessories during active vacation activities.
For vacation recommendations, distinguish between travel day, sightseeing, beach, dinner, and nightlife.
Weather should influence fabric, layering, footwear, and overall outfit practicality.
Hot weather generally favors breathable fabrics and lighter layering.
Avoid unnecessary heavy layers in high heat.
Relaxed silhouettes can improve airflow when appropriate for the occasion.
Lightweight shirts can be useful for polished summer outfits.
Footwear should allow practical movement and ventilation where appropriate.
For summer formalwear, prioritize breathable construction rather than simply removing layers.
Summer evening outfits can use lightweight darker pieces if temperature and venue allow.
Use color, fabric, and silhouette together when creating a summer look.
Do not equate summer automatically with bright colors; neutrals can also work.
Winter styling should prioritize warmth while preserving the intended silhouette.
Layering is useful for adapting outfits to cold conditions.
Outerwear should complement the base outfit in color, proportion, and formality.
Avoid adding oversized outerwear without considering the volume of the base outfit.
For formal winter outfits, structured coats can preserve professional appearance.
For casual winter outfits, jackets, overshirts, hoodies, and knitwear can provide practical layering.
Cold-weather footwear should match weather conditions and outfit formality.
Winter accessories should support the outfit rather than create unnecessary visual clutter.
Use tonal or coordinated layering when multiple winter pieces are visible.
If indoor heating is likely, consider removable layers for comfort.
Monsoon outfits should consider rain, humidity, drying time, and footwear grip.
Avoid delicate garments when significant rain exposure is expected.
Footwear should be selected for wet conditions when rain exposure is likely.
Quick-drying or practical fabrics can be preferable during humid rainy weather.
Avoid extremely long or dragging bottoms when roads and pathways may be wet.
Keep outer layers practical and easy to remove when weather changes.
For office monsoon outfits, balance professional appearance with weather practicality.
For casual monsoon outfits, prioritize practical footwear and easy-care garments.
Avoid recommending suede or other weather-sensitive materials when heavy rain exposure is expected.
If weather conditions are unknown, do not assume heavy rain and unnecessarily restrict the outfit.
Daytime outfits generally allow lighter, fresher, and more breathable styling.
Evening outfits can support deeper colors, stronger contrast, and more polished accessories.
The same outfit can often transition from day to night through footwear and layering.
Do not use time of day as the only factor when determining formality.
Outdoor daytime events should account for heat and sunlight.
Indoor evening events may allow heavier layers than outdoor daytime events.
Evening casual outfits should remain comfortable if the activity involves significant movement.
Formal evening events usually require more refinement than casual daytime events.
Use venue and dress code alongside time of day before recommending major changes.
When transitioning an outfit from day to night, prioritize one or two deliberate changes.
Streetwear often emphasizes relaxed proportions, layering, graphic or minimal statement pieces, and sneakers.
Streetwear styling should maintain intentional proportion even when silhouettes are oversized.
Baggy bottoms can be balanced with fitted, boxy, or intentionally oversized tops depending on the desired silhouette.
Avoid combining excessive oversized volume without considering overall proportions.
Sneakers are a common foundation for streetwear but should match the visual direction.
Layering can strengthen streetwear styling when each layer has a clear visual role.
Accessories should reinforce the streetwear direction rather than compete with the main garment.
Minimal streetwear can use neutral colors and restrained branding.
Statement streetwear can use one strong graphic, color, or accessory while keeping supporting pieces simpler.
Streetwear is not automatically suitable for formal, conservative, or traditional occasions.
Minimalist style prioritizes simplicity, clean lines, restrained colors, and intentional details.
Minimalist outfits should avoid unnecessary graphic, color, or accessory overload.
High-quality-looking basics can create a premium minimalist appearance without excessive branding.
Minimalist styling should still consider fit and silhouette rather than relying only on neutral colors.
A simple outfit can gain refinement through clean footwear and controlled accessories.
Use repetition of a color family to create visual continuity in minimalist outfits.
Avoid unnecessary layering when a clean single-layer outfit already satisfies the occasion.
Minimalist does not mean boring; texture, silhouette, and small details can provide interest.
For minimalist formalwear, prioritize tailoring and garment condition.
For minimalist casualwear, prioritize comfortable basics with deliberate proportions.
Classic style emphasizes timeless silhouettes, restrained patterns, and versatile garments.
Classic outfits generally benefit from clean shirts, trousers, chinos, knitwear, loafers, or simple sneakers.
Avoid excessive trend elements when the goal is a timeless appearance.
Neutral colors and traditional garment combinations are commonly useful for classic styling.
Classic styling can incorporate modern fits as long as the overall appearance remains coherent.
A classic outfit should prioritize garment quality, fit, and coordination over visible branding.
Layering with sweaters, overshirts, jackets, or blazers can support classic styling.
Avoid mixing unrelated aesthetic eras unless intentionally creating a fashion-forward look.
Classic style can be adapted for casual, office, date, and semi-formal occasions.
When the user requests a timeless outfit, prioritize versatile pieces over highly seasonal trends.
Premium-looking style should prioritize fit, fabric appearance, coordination, and restraint.
Excessive visible branding can reduce a minimalist premium appearance.
Clean footwear and controlled accessories can elevate a basic outfit.
Neutral and deep tones can support a refined appearance when coordinated correctly.
Premium-looking does not require expensive clothing; coordination and condition are important contributors.
Avoid excessive decorative elements when the intended direction is understated luxury.
Structured outerwear can elevate an otherwise simple outfit.
Accessories should look intentional and proportionate to the outfit.
Wrinkles, visible damage, and poorly maintained footwear can reduce perceived refinement.
When recommending premium-looking style, do not claim that an item is expensive unless its price is known.
For fashion content creation, the outfit should communicate its intended style clearly on camera.
Content outfits can use stronger visual contrast than ordinary everyday outfits when appropriate.
Avoid excessive visual clutter when the clothing itself is the main subject of the content.
For outfit comparison content, keep the comparison variable clear and avoid changing multiple unrelated elements.
For fashion reels, silhouette and footwear should remain visible enough to communicate the outfit.
For close-up fashion content, prioritize visible upper-body details and accessories.
For full-body outfit content, footwear and trouser length should be considered part of the visual composition.
Content styling should remain wearable unless the user explicitly requests editorial experimentation.
If the goal is product promotion, keep the product visually identifiable.
When recommending an outfit for social media, distinguish camera impact from real-world occasion suitability.
Prefer modifying one or two elements before replacing the entire outfit.
Footwear is one of the fastest ways to change perceived outfit formality.
Layering can shift an outfit between casual, smart casual, and more refined directions.
Accessories can add personality without requiring a complete outfit change.
A casual outfit can often be upgraded by replacing athletic footwear with refined footwear.
A formal outfit can often be relaxed by removing structured layers and using simpler footwear.
Changing the outer layer can adapt an outfit to different temperatures and occasions.
A single neutral base outfit can support multiple styling directions through accessories and footwear.
Do not recommend changing an item that is already suitable unless there is a clear improvement.
When adapting an outfit, preserve the user's preferred silhouette when possible.
Explicit dress codes should take priority over generic occasion rules.
If the invitation states a dress code, interpret recommendations around that requirement.
When dress code terminology is unfamiliar, explain the expected level of formality in simple language.
Do not assume that every workplace uses the same definition of business casual.
Do not treat smart casual as a universal fixed uniform; venue context matters.
If dress code and cultural expectations differ, acknowledge both factors.
For uncertain dress codes, recommend a middle-ground outfit that can be adjusted easily.
A removable jacket or overshirt can provide flexibility when dress code expectations are uncertain.
Keep formal recommendations proportionate to the actual event rather than automatically maximizing formality.
When the user provides a reference outfit, identify which elements determine its dress-code level.
Flag an outfit when its formality clearly conflicts with the stated occasion.
Flag overly athletic styling when the event requires conventional formalwear.
Flag overly formal styling when the user explicitly wants relaxed everyday clothing.
Flag weather-inappropriate layering when weather information is available.
Flag impractical footwear when the activity requires substantial walking or wet-weather use.
Flag cultural mismatch only when there is reliable context about the event's cultural expectations.
Do not flag unconventional fashion as wrong when the user intentionally selected an expressive style.
Separate objective practicality problems from subjective style preferences.
If only one element causes the mismatch, recommend changing that element instead of rejecting the whole outfit.
Use confidence-aware language when mismatch detection depends on uncertain image interpretation.
If the occasion cannot be confidently identified, state the most likely interpretation and mention uncertainty.
Do not invent venue, weather, cultural context, or dress-code details.
If an image does not clearly show footwear, do not make strong footwear-specific claims.
If clothing details are hidden or low-resolution, avoid overconfident material or garment-type identification.
When two occasions have similar requirements, provide a flexible recommendation usable in both.
Ask for missing context only when it would materially change the recommendation.
Do not ask unnecessary questions when the image and user request already provide sufficient context.
If user preference is explicitly stated, treat it as reliable input.
If user preference is not stated, avoid assuming a specific aesthetic identity.
Recommendations should identify whether a suggestion is essential, optional, or style-dependent.
Final recommendations should identify the occasion, style direction, suitable elements, and any important adjustment.
Keep the primary recommendation concise and prioritize the changes with the highest impact.
Avoid overwhelming the user with many alternative outfits when one clear recommendation is sufficient.
When alternatives are useful, provide a small number of clearly differentiated options.
Explain why an outfit suits the occasion using observable clothing characteristics.
Do not claim guaranteed suitability because dress codes and personal preferences can vary.
If an outfit is already suitable, say so and avoid unnecessary changes.
When an outfit needs improvement, identify the smallest practical change first.
Mention confidence when image analysis is uncertain or key details are not visible.
The final recommendation should combine occasion context, style direction, formality, practicality, and user preference into one coherent result.
